body:
Parent: https://github.com/Cratis/.github/issues/24

## Context

The old corpus model installed Propagate and Sync wrappers in many repositories, enabling multi-source organization-wide fan-out. Propagation is temporarily frozen while a safer model is designed.

Current live freeze:

- 78 repository Propagate/Sync wrappers are manually disabled.
- Central reusable Propagate/Sync and Bootstrap workflows are manually disabled.
- No content was reverted; repositories carry mixed corpus revisions during the pause.

A local branch `feat/ai-corpus-propagation-control` contains an uncommitted control script/workflow and documentation for status, freeze, canary, single-source restore, and explicitly confirmed legacy restore.

## Work

- [ ] Define the authoritative source and distribution artifact: direct Git synchronization, PR sync, package/version, submodule, generated bundle, or another accepted mechanism.
- [ ] Define version pinning, repository-local overrides, compatibility, drift reporting, canary rollout, rollback, and audit evidence.
- [ ] Eliminate accidental multi-source/cascading fan-out.
- [ ] Finish and review the propagation-control toolkit with fail-closed inventory/API handling and dry-run defaults.
- [ ] Canary the replacement in one repository before fleet rollout.
- [ ] Document freeze, canary, rollout, rollback, and emergency-disable procedures.
- [ ] Decide whether old wrapper YAML is removed from targets after migration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One source/version authority is explicit.
- [ ] A target cannot silently publish its local corpus to the fleet.
- [ ] Repository-local policy has an explicit supported mechanism.
- [ ] Rollout and rollback are canaried and observable.
- [ ] Control tooling reports partial failures and exits nonzero.
- [ ] The legacy all-to-all topology cannot be restored accidentally.
- [ ] The freeze is lifted only after acceptance criteria and canary evidence are reviewed.

comments.body: Partly addressed in #69: landed the fail-closed propagation-control toolkit, snapshot-backed freeze/restore, frozen-state verification, isolated canary and single-source transitions, guarded manual workflow, retry hardening, tests, and operator documentation. Still open: choose and approve the authoritative distribution model and versioning/override policy, run and review a canary, decide wrapper retirement, and lift the live freeze only after the remaining acceptance criteria are met.

Maintainer direction for the Cratis AI redesign is now accepted for execution as **Option A+**:

- `Cratis/AI` remains the canonical authoring, composition, approval, evaluation, and generation repository.
- The mixed authoring repository is not a supported public installation target.
- Approved public capabilities are generated into a dedicated automation-managed public distribution repository.
- The distribution repository is bot-owned, protected, and not manually authored.
- Immutable tags, archives, passive npm packages, native wrappers, and marketplace submissions derive from one staged logical tree.
- A separately authored public product repository is only a fallback if real host governance makes generated distribution impossible without weakening this boundary.
- `Cratis/Workflows` owns promotion, canaries, pins, rollback, emergency disable, and legacy propagation retirement.

The maintainer has also authorized autonomous execution of the redesign program: technical/product decisions, reviewable branches and pull requests, schemas, catalogs, generators, pilots, and distribution setup may proceed when their gates pass. That authority does not bypass credentials, protected-environment/vendor/legal review, destructive production authorization, or immutable-history protections.

This resolves the architecture-selection part of this issue. Keep the issue open for implementation, protected repository setup, canary evidence, version/override policy, rollback evidence, wrapper retirement, and lifting the live freeze.

title: Replace all-to-all AI corpus propagation with a controlled distribution model
